conclusion.justification: The report explicitly states that the claim is not supported by evidence and that ibuprofen does not appear to worsen COVID-19, citing multiple large studies and health authority positions. Therefore, it clearly rejects the claim.
conclusion.label: rejects

report:
**Conclusion: This claim is not supported by the evidence — ibuprofen does not appear to worsen COVID-19.**

The idea originated from a March 2020 tweet by the French health minister and a letter hypothesizing that NSAIDs might upregulate ACE2 receptors (the SARS-CoV-2 entry point), based on a single animal study in diabetic rats with no confirming human data (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7287029/). This triggered a global scare, but subsequent rigorous research has not substantiated it.

Multiple large studies contradict the claim:
- A nationwide study found no significant association between ibuprofen prescription claims and severe COVID-19 outcomes (ICU admission, respiratory failure, death) (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7537121/).
- A large multicenter cohort of 78,674 hospitalized UK patients found NSAID use was not associated with worse in-hospital mortality, critical care admission, or need for ventilation (https://www.thelancet.com/journals/lanrhe/article/PIIS2665-9913(21)00104-1/fulltext).
- A 38-center US study using data from over 857,000 COVID-19 patients (National COVID Cohort Collaborative) similarly found no worsened outcomes with NSAID use (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9107579/).

Health authorities reversed early cautious guidance after review. The WHO examined 73 studies and found no evidence NSAIDs worsen COVID-19 outcomes, a position echoed by Health Canada and the FDA (https://www.who.int/news-room/commentaries/detail/the-use-of-non-steroidal-anti-inflammatory-drugs-(nsaids)-in-patients-with-covid-19; https://www.fda.gov/drugs/drug-alerts-and-statements/fda-advises-patients-use-non-steroidal-anti-inflammatory-drugs-nsaids-covid-19).

**Bottom line:** The ibuprofen-worsens-COVID-19 claim stemmed from a plausible but unconfirmed biological hypothesis and anecdotal reports, not solid data. Large-scale epidemiological studies and major health authorities have since found no credible evidence supporting it, and ibuprofen is considered safe for symptomatic COVID-19 treatment.
